utterances.text: It would be interesting to know the date Ms. Rehn saw these bodies scattered on the ground. I have a feeling in advance that this has strictly nothing to do with the investigation I was dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it have something to do with the locality? Do you know that in the area of Bare there were over 600 combat casualties? Did you see any video footage of that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't and so what? I mean, what's the connection with these 600 combatants lying on the ground and this Srebrenica investigation? I don't see any connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, with all due respect, the two of us here are not trying to establish the importance of this or that. We're trying to establish facts. Did you know and did you see that in that area there were over 600 combat casualties? I'm not asking you anything else. Yes or no? You are fighting for the case of the Prosecution, and that's not what you're asked to do.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am fighting for nothing. I assist establishing a process of truth, and this process of truth, as far as I am concerned, is connected with the investigation I and others conducted during -- I during six years, others for another period of time, and what I can state clearly is that these 600 combatants have no connection with the investigation. This is why we did not deal with the localisation and exhumation of the mass grave in which these combatants were exhumed at Bare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let me put this this way: At one point in time today you probably said one of your goals of your investigation was to find out what happened to those 8.000 people who were missing after the fall of enclave Srebrenica. Among these 8.000 people, would you exclude that this 600, or whatever the number may be, the casualties in Bare, could have been included?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. To be more precise on the goal, the goal was not -- I mean, the initial goal was to check the rumour of these 8.000 disappearances. The goal of the investigation was to determine what happened to those who entered a criminal aspect of the war, not to -- and this number we will now know it only once the entire process is finished. The goal was not to determine the fate of those among this mass of people who were either killed in minefields, crossings them, or shot in combat operations, or maybe the few who committed suicide, and so on. It's only focusing on the criminal aspect of this episode of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Ruez, there is no grave related to these 600 men in Bare. There is no other grave. They were buried in the graves that you investigated. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that checking the dates would show that what you say is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, in your view, how many combatants did the 28th Division have? Not how many rifles, how many combatants?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea, but to make sure this bit doesn't become an issue, I could even say that all the men were combatants, potential combatants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take a break now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, this is where we were: You said that in that situation, every able-bodied man was considered to be a combatant. Do you know how many men the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had registered out of the men who imagined to get out, that is to say, the military-aged men?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. D01998. Could we have a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put the English translation on the ELMO, or has it been uploaded?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree -- actually, let's see the original, and then let's have the proper page in English. So this is a bulletin of the Military Intelligence Service of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the 17th of July, 1995. And could we now focus on -- on the English version altogether. Can we just remove the Serbian version and enlarge the English version. Do you agree that it says here that in the early evening hours of the 16th of July, 1995, approximately 10.000 members of the 28th Division arrived in the free territory [In English] "As the main body of these forces was carrying out a breakthrough." [Interpretation] And it says that this breakthrough was assisted by units of the 24th Division which launched a fierce counter-attack against Serbs or, rather, Chetnik lines in the Baljkovica sector and so on. Did anybody warn you about that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the figure I was given at that time was 6.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that they did not have more than 6.000 rifles, but as for fighting men they had a lot more? So at each and every point in time there could have been 6.000 of them that were armed; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look at 65 ter 23546. Is it correct that the investigation started already on the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So even before the fall of Srebrenica, the investigation started; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I what I say is the -- the investigation focused on events that started once the enclave fell. So this is 11 July, around 12 -- 12.00. It's not that as soon as 11 July an investigation started. It's the date that is the starting point of the events that then became the focus of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's clearer to me now. When did you start the investigation? When were you given this assignment?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The precise date I do not remember. It was probably somewhere around the 15, I would think, and then arrival to the first mission area that was Tuzla I think was the 20 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that His Excellency Mr. Akashi recommended caution as regards the number of missing persons?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about his recommendation, but cautious -- caution is the essence when you approach such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I suggest that we remove the Serbian version so that we can see the English version better. Please, do you agree that this is a telegram from Ambassador Akashi on the 19th of July to Mr. Annan, who was Under-Secretary for military operations at the time, and that this pertains to the following: Missing persons from Srebrenica or displaced persons from Srebrenica displaced to the area around Tuzla and Tuzla itself.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 2 where these people were accommodated and who organised all of it. The joint action crisis team put up 600 -- or 6.000 in the Tuzla air base, BiH local authorities report that 18.333 are accommodated in collective centres, and they are distributed as follows -- around Tuzla; right? And roughly that is about 25.000 altogether; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then in paragraph 3, it says -- it says that this arithmetic is based on an estimate that in Srebrenica the population was about 42.000. So it would seem that 17.000 were unaccounted for, and do you agree that 13- to 15.000 were involved in this breakthrough through the woods?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe you will disagree if I were to say to you that there were 37.000 of them in 1994 and that that was the highest figure. After that, in July 1995, there were considerably less. Do you know that Oric lost about 2.000 fighting men before July? So out of this estimated figure of 37.000, from the beginning of 1994 until 1995, he lost about 1.000 fighting men, so that would total about 36.000; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please take a look at what His Excellency Mr. Akashi says in terms of this arithmetic. So could we look at the next page now, please. At the top here he says that the unaccounted for would be 4- to 8.000, but he says: [In English] "Due to the imprecise nature of these figures, we recommend that any public statements are limited to the broad reference of several thousand missing." [Interpretation] On the 19th of July, Mr. Akashi recommends caution because the numbers game could fire back or lead to undesirable consequences; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right. This is why the list of missing people from Srebrenica made by the ICRC could only be valid once the exchange of prisoners process was totally finalised in March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that about 1.000 inhabitants, most of them combatants from the 28th Division but inhabitants of Srebrenica, fled to Serbia via Zepa? They were taken in and put up in reception centres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I have some foundation for that question? I don't think that's in any way supported by the evidence that a thousand people fled to Zepa and then to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, right now I'm not tendering that as evidence. I'm asking this witness whether he based his opinion and findings, including this incoming figure, on that. If -- I mean, that is quite provable, and I will prove that, but let him answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I can make my objection more specific. We don't contest that a thousand-plus men from Zepa went across the river to Serbia in late July. The part I object to or want some foundation for is that those men originally came from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now, having heard Mr. Mitchell's objection, please reformulate your question, Mr. Karadzic, or is it your case that those 1.000 people were from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I claim that from Srebrenica they went to Zepa and from Zepa to Serbia, and in the case of President Milosevic, evidence was provided and I am going to provide that evidence too. At this point in time, I'm interested in asking whether Mr. Ruez had that information available and whether that contributed to his findings, whether that was one of the elements involved when he was drawing his own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Now can you answer the question, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At one point, I think in 1996, we indeed came across an information that a group, unspecified number, of persons from Srebrenica succeeded reaching the other bank of the Drina and reached Serbia. We also -- I mean, I saw a report from the Red Cross, I think, that stated that these people had been then sent back to Bosnia, so these ones were not, anyhow, sent back to Republika Srpska, at least these ones, so they exited the frame of the criminal investigation, and we didn't pursue on their part -- their possible part of the story. But I'm not sure we are talking about the same ones. We know and I already told it that one survivor of Kravica warehouse succeeded after that to flee toward Zepa where he was captured again, but not identified as coming from Srebrenica and who was in the last group of prisoners exchanged, I think, March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that after all, witnesses from the warring parties, the parties concerned, witnesses who are injured parties, require some reservation with regard to their estimated figures and other information provided. Can this be taken at face value, or does one have to have a bit of reservation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reservations regarding figures have to be taken with a lot of care from whatever side they are coming from. This is the reason why I always and continuously say that the final figure of those assassinated in the course of the Srebrenica operation will be known only once all the graves will be exhumed. All the other dead or disappeared do not enter the frame of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Actually, can you tell us, first of all, when did the Sandici meadow killing take place? You confirmed that part of the transportation could not be carried out. At what time was this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one was killed on the Sandici meadow. It was a regroupment spot for prisoners. Those who were killed coming from the Sandici meadow were killed at the Kravica warehouse. But we also know from witness testimonies that those at the end of the 13 who had no transportation to go to Bratunac were killed at the location where they were. We did not put all this in the direct presentation because they are part of the, let's say, sub -- sub-stories compared with the big picture of the organised extermination process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you rule out the possibility that there was an ambush, ambush for this Muslim column in Sandici and that some persons were killed during the fighting there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ambush you refer to was not at Sandici. It was behind the hill at the level of -- of Kravica, in the forest. The bodies of those who got killed during this military -- legitimate military operation were left at the locations where they died, and in 1996, Ms. Elizabeth Rehn you were referring to previously led a mission to recover surface remains who were still -- who had never been picked up in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But those who surrendered in Sandici did not surrender of their own free will. The surrender happened because they were fought against; right? And you can see in that footage that you provided that there is an exchange of gunfire, that the Muslims are firing from rifles and the Serbs from APCs.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's two different things. The surrender happened the day after the ambush. The ambush occurred during the night-time, but the column was also shelled, and the surrender process of the 13 was mainly due, indeed, because of a quick exhaustion process of those who surrendered, but also because they realised they had no exit-way from the location they were and also because of this convincing process of fake UN personnel on the asphalt road. The bit of the footage you refer to as the APCs firing anti-aircraft 30-millimetre ammunition on the fleeing men is in another location, but also, indeed, participates to all the reasons that led the fleers to make a surrender decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But that also happened on this road that goes from Kravica to Konjevic Polje and passes through Sandici; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Surrenders happened all along this stretch of road. The only big spots I went through during the presentation of surrender process are the main spots, but the fact is that men went out of the woods all along the stretch of road, let's say roughly from Kravica, Sandici area, indeed down to Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wasn't very specific. The fire that you refer to was elsewhere, but was it on the same road further away from Sandici towards Konjevic Polje, but it's in the same direction. It's what you can see in the footage.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. All the stretch of road going, let's say, from Bratunac to Nova Kasaba was totally blocked by 13 in the morning by the Bosnian Serb Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5025. Can we have a look at that, please? Actually, I beg your pardon. Could that cable of Mr. Akashi's be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2046, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D2505. That is what I'd like to have displayed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is part of the transcript from the Krstic case when you testified.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5025. This is page 594 in the Krstic transcript. Yes, we have it. I'm looking for page 594. I don't know what number it is in e-court, but here in the corner we should see number 594. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Start with line 16, please. This is where the question is, and then we have your answer: "[In English] First of all, we are going to view the video. The video we have put together is starting, in fact, from the ambush sites. In fact, it starts with a film from a helicopter, starting in the vicinity of the area of the village Bare, which was circled on the map, on the photocopy of the map, where shelling took place. The column was ambushed in that area, and there is still clothing to be seen on the film from the," next page, "helicopter," and so on. And then from line 8: "This area has been processed in 1996 by a team of experts from Finland who were operating in that area in 1996, totally disconnected from our activities, they were collecting surface remains. But it's important to note that 600 bodies have been collected in that area. These are bodies of victims killed in combat, in ambushes, in shellings and possibly also in other circumstances which are impossible to sort out between -- I mean, for us, at least, between combat and other situations -- situations." [Interpretation] Do you still adhere by that answer?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Totally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Irrespective of the fact whether you dealt with that or not, when I speak about the total number of inhabitants in Srebrenica and the total number of missing, do you agree that for me the 600 means something else than it does to you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said, I'm not in the brain of persons, so I'm not in yours. I could not answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with me that up to 1996, there were bodies scattered in the forest, and in this place here there was even a very large concentration of the bodies that were still not buried by that time?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I even think, but that's my personal thought, that the Bosnian Serb Army did not bother at all collecting the bodies of those who had been killed in the area. The ones who were buried were those who were en masse in the combat zones, but mainly those who were exhumed in locations that we could clearly connect with the execution sites. All the rest, probably the remains are still in the hills and the forest and scattered all around, but we will never know their number. This is why again and again the focus is on those who are found in the execution sites and in the secondary graves. And the number will only be known, unfortunately, only at the end of the full exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there is a legal obligation for the remains to be removed after every cycle of fighting and that there were civilian protection units who did that, who removed carcasses and body remains? They did it after every fighting campaign.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that there are a number of legal obligations during wartime, but I also have a feeling that the legal aspect was sometimes and most of the time forgotten during this war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, very well. A witness will come who will testify, because he was one of those who did that. Can we go to the following page. Let's start you looking at line 15. You identified people in the video, and then on line 20 you say: [In English] "In fact, the main concentration of items and bodies are in the trees, the line of trees. The number of bodies collected there in 1996, as I said, is around 600, and this is important information in order to check, in fact, the ability of many of the witnesses to assess numbers." Next page: "In this location, the assessment of victims provided by the witnesses is much more than what has been collected. The numbers usually announced in this area are 1.500 to 2.000 victims, but there is a natural inflation of the assessment of numbers of -- in these circumstances." [Interpretation] This is what you just confirmed for us. You said that witnesses sometimes tend to exaggerate; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the transcript pages be admitted? I've just displayed pages 594 through 597.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we need it? Entire passage were read out and witness confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I did read passages out so that they may be heard, and also in case you decide not to admit the transcript pages, I still wanted to have something on the record. I don't think it will be superfluous to have those pages in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The less we have, the better we'll be off. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's look at 192 from Mr. Ruez's book. That's illustration 192.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, Mr. Ruez, that all the burials of the victims who died in July 1995, had to be carried out in that month? In other words, they could not be carried out before the 5th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, clearly. We know and we went through the precise dates of all this, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Between the 5th and the 17th of July, you received the photo that we see now. Was that photo taken from the same angle, and was the light the same when the photo was taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't receive the photo between the 5th and the 17th, we received it much later, but the first one is taken the 5th, the second one the 17th. The angle, as you can see is not exactly the same one, but the -- the 5th shows how it was before the date we are concerned about, that is, 15 and the 17th. We know the burial took place the 15th. The 17th, we can see a very obvious change in the terrain in this Kozluk area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I believe, Mr. Ruez, that both you and I look different from the side and from en face. We have two different angles, one is from the side and the other is en face, as it were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were all taken direction north towards south, but with a lately different angle. The best reference point for that is the straight line of the dirt road going direction south and also at the bottom of the picture the continuous road. So we -- you just need to move it a little bit to see that it's the same direction with a slightly different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the white surface that we see in that photo taken from the side where that road depicts the outline of a nose? What's on the tip of the nose? When you look at the photo that was taken on the 5th of July, how were you able to conclude that there were no burials there prior to that date?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area has been later -- we know it's an area of gravel. A disturbance before the 5th, assumption is that it's a gravel area. For the size of the graves, the digging method of the grave, I will leave it to the archaeologists, to Professor Richard Wright, to explain the on the ground and then at the ground situation on that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, the executions and the burials were completed before the 17th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If there were sanitisation burials, they would have been carried out after the 17th of July. If there had been any, they could have only taken place after the 17th of July; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that the largest number of aerial photos were taken between the 5th or the 7th July and the 27th of July?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those we were provided with were indeed in this time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we don't know which of these changes occurred on the 11th, 19th, 20th, 21st, and on to the 26th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This photograph, however, is with a longer range, from the 5th to the 17th; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see what you mean with "longer range," sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, it's -- I meant to say it's a short interval, a short interval between the 5th to the 17th. In the other cases, the interval is longer, from the 5th to 27th. Ten days are missing. In here, those ten days are not missing.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know and did you indeed confirm that the first fighting in Srebrenica and around Srebrenica, the so-called initial task, began with the fighting in the south of the enclave where the Observation Post Echo was located?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The fighting there lasted from the 5th or the 6th of July until the 11th; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone get killed in that fighting?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there is fighting, usually there are dead people also. I don't know about it. I don't know their numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I should now like to find the map with grave sites in Zeleni Jadar. I lost it for a moment. If I can have a moment to find it. You listed them as secondary graves, Jadar, 249. Map 249. What would Serbs do with the dead Muslims, or, rather, the bodies of dead Muslims who remain on their territory in Zeleni Jadar, for instance? Is it natural to think that they would bury them if there is no exchange of bodies?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Natural, I don't know, because the 600 bodies on the hills above Kravica which were collected by the team of Elizabeth Rehn had to be collected by Elizabeth Rehn. If not, they would probably still be around, certainly not now, but because of the fact that every year now groups of people make a -- follow path from Susnjari to Nezuk on 11th July, these bodies would for sure having been removed by the commission for missing persons, but in the years following 1995, they would have stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this the area where the fighting started, the area of the main advance of the Serb troops?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the area from where the -- the Serb troops took the direction to enter Srebrenica town. It was not a main fighting spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But where did they offer the most resistance and where did the breakthrough take the longest? When they passed through Zeleni Jadar, the Muslim defence was dispersed, and they were thinking about leaving.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go in detail with the military episode of take-over, but since I understand where -- what you want to imply, let's consider this area as a battle area indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Ruez, I don't believe -- in fact, I know that the Serbs are not that thorough, not so thorough that they would take out and rebury bodies from primary graves. Those were contemporaneous graves from that time where Muslim combatants who got killed then and there were buried, or did you perhaps find other graves where they were buried?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to clarify that. Is it Mr. Karadzic's case that the six graves in Zeleni Jadar we see here contain the bodies of combat casualties killed in the fighting in the lead-up to the taking of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My case is that the Serbs buried those people somewhere, and the layout of these graves shows precisely that they were buried where they got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And I'm asking you whether you found some other graves where those who fell during the defence of the enclave, at least its southern part, were buried.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we know as a fact, and Professor Wright, who conducted exhumations on some of these sites, all of them are not exhumed yet, but those who were, he will be able to, together with Dean Manning, the scientific connections they have with the disturbed site of Glogova, the site of Glogova having contained the bodies of those killed at the Kravica warehouse, those killed during their detention in Bratunac town, and those killed alongside of the road Bratunac-Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about those who got killed while defending this southern part of the enclave? Do you have dates for this photograph 249?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If ever that burial process took place on some of these spots, we would have to wait the full exhumation of these sites in order to connect them also to Glogova. At this point we have no information of the burial process you refer to, but if this would be the case, I would believe that those who did that burial kept reports of what they did, at least to be able to show that the fuel that was consumed in that process was not sold on the black market. So there should be records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But for now we cannot make that conclusion, can we, until the process is finalised, the process of exhumation and analysis; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I always said. We need to have numbers. We need to have exhumations. And these exhumations, still in 2012, they're not all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can have the Court's indulgence until I find the map of the enclave showing Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether LiveNote is functioning at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have one, page 23 in the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's back. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we call up this page 23. May I ask you, Mr. Ruez, to take a pencil and mark the area of Zeleni Jadar where the fighting started. That's E, F, and S observation posts. Could the usher please activate the pen. Oh, you've done it yourself. Could you just put ZJ for Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one was Observation Post F, and so the area here is Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put the date, please, and your initials.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2047, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we now see the image 266. Mr. Pirocanac and, in fact, you, when you made these photographs, you paid due attention to the mosques in Srebrenica; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact not so much, because as I said, there are three mosques in Srebrenica. I happened to take photographs mainly of two of them, in one by passing by, and the other one could indeed witness the slow destruction process of it, but the third one, for example, we never made any attempt even to find where it was and what happened to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the church here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. As I said, there were two religious monuments in centre town, the mosque and the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know what the church looked like until July 1995? Maybe you saw part of it in that footage, that it had no bell-tower and no roof. Do you know what it was converted into before July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The only thing I can see on the photograph is that the mosque is now a pile of rubble and the church is still standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when was this photo taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, I think, was taken in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And if I tell you that on the 4th of August, 1995, I saw this church, it had no roof and a good part of the bell-tower was missing, it had been converted into a stable or a cattle shed and a public toilet, would you believe me?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so. I have no reason not to believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope you understand I'm not trying to justify anything. I'm only trying to gain insight into the motives, into the causes and consequences, which doesn't make what happened any less ugly. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not more agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we see again the transcript 1D5025. You were aware, weren't you, that civilians were able to and dared to stay there to meet the Serbs, whereas some others feared Serb revenge; correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look at page 492. From line 4 on, you say that some people fell -- felt they had nothing to hide, and the inference seems to be that those who left did not have the same feeling and they went through the mountains into -- towards Udrc. That's page -- or lines 17 and 18.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we scroll down a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what these mountains look like, how forbidding that terrain is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the landscape?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That stretch from Srebrenica to -- to Tuzla, especially the Udrc mountain. Do you agree it was a very impassable and forbidding area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, and this is the reason why this area was selected, because it was maybe difficult to cross, but there they were also difficult to chase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look at the next page. You were aware that the existence of that column and the fact that they were trying to break out was a surprise to the Serbs, and they had to be concerned about what this column of 15.000 men would do; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have the information that I, at the request of the local civilian authorities, after the so-called victory in Srebrenica on the 11th of July, had to proclaim the state of war on the 14th of July in those several municipalities to make the situation more serious, to get the defence to -- to become more serious? Do you know that I proclaimed a state of war on the 14th of July, after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know, but I can only say it was a wise decision, since General Mladic had taken an opposite one, which was to move his forces towards Zepa without, indeed, considering the military threat that this column of mainly military people for its spearhead could do on its trip towards the BiH territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In lines 10 onwards, for instance in line 16: [In English] "On July the 12th, once the Bosnian Serb Army realised what in fact was happening, which was that a huge column of men was trying to flee the area and indeed take this direction. Initially there was an element of surprise, so no possibility to challenge that column. Part of that column was armed. The first group was organised in brigades. The forces inside Srebrenica were quite structured, and they recreated brigades at the -- at the moment they were assembling. Those who had weapons were mainly walking in front." [Interpretation] So you were perfectly well aware that the 28th Division was organised into several brigades and that they restructured and reestablished those brigades when the column started to break out.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. This is why all the actions on the line of fled of this unit is -- has to be considered as a legitimate combat operation and is not investigated in the frame of the criminal investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at the next page: [In English] "Here it shows battles which took place in this location. I won't deal with that also, but around the 13th and 14th of July --" [Interpretation] It's about that fighting. Could we then see line 21 onwards: [In English] "Once they arrived in the area here which is the south-west of Zvornik, ambushes were set to block this column, but these ambushes were not successful. In fact, the column punched through these Serbs position, managed to capture equipment, anti-aircraft," can we see the next page, "guns, mortars, and even manages to capture Serb prisoners." [Interpretation] Do you agree, Mr. Ruez, that the Serb side was in ambushes and in trenches and suffered horrendous losses and the side that was not in trenches and not on the attack suffered even more horrific losses?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. We found out later that the Zvornik Brigade -- I don't know how many personnel they -- they lost during these few days, but I heard it was more than during all the rest of the war. But then it's a question of military experts to -- to know why all these Serb soldiers ended dead when the military operation, on the other hand, was supposed to be a full success, full and easy success. But Mladic, as I said, had the decision to move towards Zepa, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, is it time to adjourn?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that we could go a bit more if you like.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If parties would not object, can we go to 2.00 today?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It's fine with us, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Registry, is it okay? Yes, please continue. We'll adjourn at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellencies. These pages from 942 to 945 may they be admitted, all of them, because I haven't actually read all of it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That being your request, there's no reason not to admit it. Yes that will be admitted as --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2048, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us briefly cast a glance at -- I beg your pardon. You spoke about this funeral in Branjevo, but let me just find the number of this picture. The caption reads "Funeral at Branjevo." What did you mean when you called it "Funeral in Branjevo"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope it is interpretation and not translation, because I hardly hear myself using the word "funeral" for a mass burial of executed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two hundred nine, and then we'll leaf through the rest. And on page 36 -- no, yesterday, the 31st of January, you said that this was a burial at Branjevo Farm; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the process is ending at this moment. There are still bodies left on the -- on the surface. The -- the grave is not closed yet, but this inhumation was completed, according to the engineer unit's log. Inhumation was completed that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you something for the remainder of our time today and then we're going to deal with other things tomorrow. Were you a professional throughout your work there, or were you involved a bit emotionally and politically?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assessment of my way of doing won't be done by myself but by all the public sources of what I had to say about this case. So I leave it to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But the Defence is a bit concerned when they see that someone is very fired up when doing a job when it should be done with a cool head. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, what you're asking the witness to agree with, that the Defence is concerned or whether somebody should keep a cool head? It would be -- the question amounts to a trap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Don't worry. I don't feel trapped. What -- what you name someone heated up, I must agree that, yes, when you investigate on a situation that ends up in legal terms named not extermination but genocide, the least you can do is to be fully heated up, being obsessed by finalising the case and providing all the elements that make the situation solid in the eyes of history.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 1D5022. Could we have that, please. You gave an interview in 2001 to "Monitor," a Montenegrin magazine; right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Already in the first question does it not say -- are you not asked, actually, whether you were fanatical about the job that you were performing? Do you remember this interview?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do you agree that the interview started with the journalist's impression that you were fanatical about the job?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the job, yes. About doing the job and completing the job, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the bottom of the page, it says: [In English] "At some point, it gives you intimate knowledge of the feeling of the people who experience it all. Then you get to know the terrain, each shrub, and sometimes you get the impression that you even know things you don't."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reason why you have not to be under the impression of what you feel, your personal feeling and instinct, but you have to stick to what the people say and build what I name the walls of this investigation, that is, corroborate or infirm the declarations of these victims. This is the cold-blood, cold-brain aspect you were referring to previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the next page. Please take a look at this last answer towards the bottom. [No interpretation]: [In English] "I can say no more, but so far we have not established the participation of Belgrade in Srebrenica. This does not mean that it had no part in ... or that it didn't have knowledge of it."

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should, in that case, not take this only sentence but read all the rest also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm interested in is the following: Irrespective of speculations as to who Mladic could have had ties to, does it not say here that you did not have any evidence of the participation of official Belgrade in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time this interview was given, we had not yet accessed the video-tape named the video of the Skorpion, this Serb military unit that was in Rogatica and who received the delivery of six young men of Srebrenica, the only aside the three seconds of footage at Kravica show the entire ordeal of these young men who are assassinated live on this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient, we can adjourn for today, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue tomorrow at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of February, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.58 p.m.,
